daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Performance Rankings with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a SQL query that ranks stocks by their year-to-date percentage return using window functions. Calculate for each stock: (1) ROW_NUMBER() ranked by YTD return descending, (2) the percentage change from start of year to most recent date, (3) LAG() to show the previous trading day's close price for comparison, (4) a running average of the last 20 trading days using a window frame. Filter to show only the top 20 performers and bottom 10 performers. Expected output: 30 rows with columns: stock_symbol, ytd_return_pct, rank, previous_close, twenty_day_moving_avg, trading_date.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning and Feature Engineering
daily_quests.description: Download the NSW Road Crash Data from data.nsw.gov.au. Write a Python script using pandas that: (1) loads the crash CSV file, (2) handles missing values intelligently (document your strategy for each column), (3) converts date/time columns to datetime objects, (4) extracts features like day_of_week, hour_of_day, is_nighttime (between 22:00-06:00), and severity_category (group injury levels), (5) removes duplicates based on crash_id, (6) exports a cleaned CSV with only relevant columns. Expected output: a cleaned CSV file with at least 15 columns and a summary report showing null counts before/after cleaning and row counts before/after deduplication.

daily_quests.title: AIHW Health Expenditure Analysis: Python ETL + SQL Analytics
daily_quests.description: Working with AIHW health expenditure data: (1) Use Python to extract and clean the health expenditure CSV (handle currency formats, missing values, and inconsistent state abbreviations), normalise state names to standard two-letter codes (NSW, VIC, QLD, etc.), and load the cleaned data into a SQLite database with appropriate schema and indexes. (2) Write SQL queries to: calculate total health spending by state and year, use a CTE to rank states by spending growth rate year-over-year, and create a window function query showing each state's spending as a percentage of national total, with a RANK() of states by their percentage share. (3) Output: a cleaned CSV, a SQLite .db file, and a results CSV containing the window function output (state, year, spending, pct_of_national, rank). Expected deliverables: 3 files demonstrating full data pipeline from raw to analytics-ready.
